description: The suppletive adjectival triples of Table 4.1: positive, comparative and superlative forms as printed, each triple with the root classes Bobaljik assigns its grades. A triple counts once however many languages share it (section 1.3).

root_classes.comment: Giazza is in the Tredici Comuni; Glottocode of Tredici Comuni Cimbrian
footnote a: the source gives no superlative; Sorbian superlatives prefix naj- to the comparative. The book does not say which Sorbian; Glottocode of the family
footnote b: Romance keeps the comparatives but no synthetic superlative
footnote c: the later Goidelic languages lack a distinct superlative
footnote d (footnote 2 of the chapter): the two defective triples counted as one ABC triple, perhaps unwisely
the comparative is printed weh/wah-īy and kept as printed
the one problematic ABA, a doublet in some varieties (section 4.1.2)
footnote e: k’argi-i formed a regular comparative in Old Georgian
footnote f: the xo-...-a forms are used with a positive sense and may not belong here

footnote g: Modern Greek keeps the comparative, with a periphrastic superlative
footnote h: some sources give further doublets
